message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"6","text":"For if you become occupied with the cares of ordinary life, you will lay a snare both for yourself and for your hearers. For because your occupations leave you unable to equip them with what is beneficial, you will be punished for not teaching what is beneficial, while those who did not learn will perish, ignorance being the cause. Therefore, give them your undistracted time and preside over them, so that at the right time you may provide words capable of saving them. And so let them heed you, knowing that whatever the ambassador of the truth binds on earth has also been bound in heaven, and whatever he looses has been loosed. You, however, will bind what must be bound and loose what must be loosed. These, then, and things like them are the duties that concern you as the presiding officer.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"βιωτικαῖς μερίμναις ἀσχοληθῇς","chosen":"become occupied with the cares of ordinary life","rationale":"βιωτικός concerns everyday worldly life, while ἀσχολέομαι emphasizes being occupied and deprived of leisure."},{"source_quote":"τὰ συμφέροντα ἐφοδιάζειν","chosen":"equip them with what is beneficial","rationale":"ἐφοδιάζω depicts supplying provisions or equipment; the implied recipients are the hearers."},{"source_quote":"εὐσχολῶν προκαθέσθητι","chosen":"give them your undistracted time and preside over them","rationale":"εὐσχολέω contrasts with prior preoccupation, while προκαθέζομαι denotes taking the leading or presiding position."},{"source_quote":"ὁ τῆς ἀληθείας πρεσβευτὴς","chosen":"the ambassador of the truth","rationale":"πρεσβευτής denotes an authorized envoy or ambassador, not merely an elder."},{"source_quote":"δέδεται καὶ ἐν οὐρανῷ","chosen":"has also been bound in heaven","rationale":"The Greek perfect is retained rather than harmonized with a familiar future-tense biblical rendering."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"οἱ δὲ μὴ μαθόντες ἀγνοίας αἰτία ἀπολοῦνται","issue":"The printed nominative αἰτία is syntactically abrupt. It can be understood parenthetically, “ignorance being the cause,” as translated, though a dative expressing cause is an evident possible conjecture.","proposed_reading":"οἱ δὲ μὴ μαθόντες ἀγνοίας αἰτίᾳ ἀπολοῦνται","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"καὶ τὰ μὲν. κατὰ σὲ","issue":"The printed full stop interrupts the construction joining μὲν with κατὰ σέ. The translation treats this as continuous sense while retaining the supplied words.","proposed_reading":"καὶ τὰ μὲν κατὰ σὲ","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"7","text":"Let the duties concerning the elders be these: above all, let them quickly join the young in marriage, forestalling the snares of youthful desire. But let them not neglect marriage even for those already old, for in some people desire remains vigorous even after they have grown old. Therefore, so that sexual immorality may not gain ground against you and bring the same plague upon you, take precautions beforehand and investigate whether the fire of adultery may be springing up secretly among you. For adultery is a very terrible thing—so terrible that it holds second place in punishment, since first place is awarded to those who are in error, even if they are chaste. Therefore, as elders of the church, train Christ’s bride in chastity (and by “bride” I mean the corporate body of the church). For if she is found chaste by the bridegroom king, she will obtain the greatest honor, and you, as those invited to the wedding, will enjoy great rejoicing. But if she is discovered to have sinned, she will be cast out, and you will pay the penalty if perhaps the sin came about through your neglect.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"πρὸς γάμον ζευγνύτωσαν","chosen":"let them join the young in marriage","rationale":"ζευγνύω literally joins or yokes together and here refers to arranging marriage."},{"source_quote":"τῆς νεαζούσης ἐπιθυμίας τὰ παγιδεύματα","chosen":"the snares of youthful desire","rationale":"The rendering preserves the trapping image of παγίδευμα and treats νεάζουσα as characterizing desire associated with youth."},{"source_quote":"ἡ πορνεία νομὴν λαβοῦσα καθ’ ὑμῶν","chosen":"sexual immorality may ... gain ground against you","rationale":"νομὴν λαμβάνειν can describe spreading or gaining range, especially of disease or fire; “gain ground” retains that image."},{"source_quote":"τὰ δευτερεῖα ἔχειν αὐτὴν τῆς κολάσεως","chosen":"it holds second place in punishment","rationale":"δευτερεῖα denotes the second rank or prize; the ranking metaphor is retained."},{"source_quote":"τοῖς ἐν πλάνῃ οὖσιν","chosen":"those who are in error","rationale":"πλάνη may denote doctrinal or moral error, but the text does not explicitly narrow its reference."},{"source_quote":"τῆς ἐκκλησίας τὸ σύστημα","chosen":"the corporate body of the church","rationale":"σύστημα denotes an organized whole or collective body rather than a building."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"8","text":"Therefore, above all, concern yourselves with chastity, for sexual immorality has been decreed exceedingly grave in God’s sight. There are many kinds of sexual immorality, as Clement himself will explain to you. But the first is adultery: a man’s not having relations only with his own wife, and a woman’s not having relations only with her own husband. If someone is chaste, he can also become benevolent, and for this he will obtain eternal mercy. Just as adultery is a great evil, so benevolence is the greatest good. Therefore love all your brothers with reverent and merciful eyes, doing for orphans what parents do and for widows what husbands do, providing with complete gladness their food, marriages for those in their prime, and, for those among them without a trade, devising through occupations the means of necessary sustenance: work for a craftsperson, mercy for one unable to work.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"παρὰ τῷ θεῷ χαλεπὴ ὥρισται ἡ πορνεία","chosen":"sexual immorality has been decreed exceedingly grave in God’s sight","rationale":"ὁρίζω indicates authoritative determination, while χαλεπή here describes severity or gravity."},{"source_quote":"πρώτη μοιχεία ἐστὶν","chosen":"the first is adultery","rationale":"πρώτη is understood as the first of the previously mentioned kinds of sexual immorality, without adding “worst.”"},{"source_quote":"τὸ ἄνδρα μὴ ἰδίᾳ μόνῃ χρήσασθαι γυναικὶ","chosen":"a man’s not having relations only with his own wife","rationale":"χρῆσθαι with a spouse in this sexual context denotes marital or sexual relations; a literal “use” would mislead in English."},{"source_quote":"φιλάνθρωπος ... φιλανθρωπία","chosen":"benevolent ... benevolence","rationale":"These words describe humane generosity or care for others and are distinguished from the explicit command ἀγαπᾶτε, rendered “love.”"},{"source_quote":"τοῖς αὐτῶν ἀτέχνοις διὰ τῶν ἐπιτηδευμάτων ἐννοούμενοι τὰς προφάσεις τῆς ἀναγκαίας τροφῆς","chosen":"for those among them without a trade, devising through occupations the means of necessary sustenance","rationale":"αὐτῶν is taken partitively, ἀτέχνοις as people lacking a trade, and προφάσεις as practical means or opportunities rather than deceptive pretexts."},{"source_quote":"τεχνίτῃ ἔργον, ἀδρανεῖ ἔλεος","chosen":"work for a craftsperson, mercy for one unable to work","rationale":"The compressed contrast assigns work to one capable of a craft and charitable aid to the inactive or incapacitated; ἀδρανής can also mean idle."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"9","text":"I know that you will do these things if you establish love in your mind. For its entry there is one sufficient occasion: sharing salt together. Therefore make every effort to dine with one another as often as you can, so that you do not barter it away; for it is the cause of doing good, and doing good is the cause of salvation. All of you, then, make your means of life common to everyone who is a brother according to God, knowing that by giving temporary things you will receive eternal things. All the more, feed the hungry and provide drink to the thirsty, clothing to the naked; visit the sick; show yourselves to those in prison and help them as you can; receive strangers into your own homes with complete eagerness. But, so that I do not speak item by item, benevolence will teach you to do every good thing, just as misanthropy points out the practice of evil to those who do not wish to be saved.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἡ κοινὴ τῶν ἁλῶν μετάληψις","chosen":"sharing salt together","rationale":"The expression evokes shared food and table fellowship while preserving the source’s specific image of salt."},{"source_quote":"πυκνότερον συνέστιοι ἀλλήλων γίνεσθαι","chosen":"dine with one another as often as you can","rationale":"σύνεστιος describes people sharing a table or household meal, and πυκνότερον indicates increased frequency."},{"source_quote":"αὐτὴν μὴ ἀπεμπολήσητε","chosen":"so that you do not barter it away","rationale":"The pronoun refers to love, and ἀπεμπολέω supplies a commercial image of selling or trading something away."},{"source_quote":"κοινοὺς ... τοὺς ἑαυτῶν παρέχετε βίους","chosen":"make your means of life common","rationale":"βίος can denote livelihood, resources, or material means; the context of giving favors this over merely living together."},{"source_quote":"τοῖς ἐν φυλακαῖς ἐπιφαινόμενοι","chosen":"show yourselves to those in prison","rationale":"ἐπιφαίνομαι literally means to appear or make oneself visible; the rendering preserves that nuance rather than reducing it entirely to “visit.”"},{"source_quote":"τὸ κατ᾽ εἶδος λέγω","chosen":"speak item by item","rationale":"κατ’ εἶδος here means treating matters individually by kind or category."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"10","text":"Brothers who have disputes must not have them adjudicated before the authorities, but must in every way be brought to agreement by the elders of the church, readily obeying them. Moreover, flee greed, since under the pretext of temporary gain it can deprive you of eternal good things. Do you carefully observe fair balances, measures, weights, and the just standards of the various localities? Act honorably with regard to deposits entrusted to you. Moreover, you will persevere in doing these and similar things to the end if you keep in your hearts an inseparable remembrance of the judgment that comes from God. For who could sin while fully convinced that a judgment by the righteous God—who for now is only patient and good—has been appointed to take place at life’s end, so that the good may thereafter enjoy the inexpressible good things everlastingly, while those found to be sinners will, as evil people, receive inexpressible punishment throughout the age? And if the prophet of the truth had not said under oath that these things would be so, it might perhaps have been reasonable to doubt.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"οἱ πράγματα ἔχοντες ἀδελφοὶ","chosen":"brothers who have disputes","rationale":"πράγματα ἔχειν in this legal setting refers to having cases, grievances, or disputes rather than simply being busy."},{"source_quote":"ὑπὸ τῶν τῆς ἐκκλησίας πρεσβυτέρων συμβιβαζέσθωσαν","chosen":"must ... be brought to agreement by the elders of the church","rationale":"συμβιβάζω here concerns reconciliation or settlement between disputants."},{"source_quote":"ζυγά, μέτρα, σταθμία, τὰ τῶντόπων δίκαια ἐπιμελῶς φυλάσσετε;","chosen":"Do you carefully observe fair balances, measures, weights, and the just standards of the various localities?","rationale":"The supplied edition’s question mark is represented as a question; φυλάσσετε can formally be either indicative or imperative."},{"source_quote":"πρὸς τὰς παρακαταθήκας εὐγνωμονεῖτε","chosen":"Act honorably with regard to deposits entrusted to you","rationale":"In relation to entrusted property, εὐγνωμονέω denotes conscientious, fair, or honorable conduct rather than simple gratitude."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ νῦν μόνου μακροθύμου καὶ ἀγαθοῦ","chosen":"who for now is only patient and good","rationale":"This takes μόνου predicatively with the present description of God. The wording could alternatively be understood as saying that God alone is now patient and good."},{"source_quote":"τῶν ἀπορρήτων ἀγαθῶν ... ἀπορρήτου κολάσεως","chosen":"the inexpressible good things ... inexpressible punishment","rationale":"The same adjective ἀπόρρητος is rendered consistently on both sides of the contrast."},{"source_quote":"ἀιδίως ... τὸν αἰῶνα","chosen":"everlastingly ... throughout the age","rationale":"The translation preserves the source’s shift from the adverb ἀιδίως to the accusative temporal expression τὸν αἰῶνα, which can also function idiomatically in the sense “forever.”"}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"τῶντόπων","issue":"The supplied print joins the article and noun without a space. This is an orthographic word-division feature and does not create substantive textual uncertainty.","proposed_reading":"τῶν τόπων","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"ἵνα οἱ ἀγαθοὶ τοῦ λοιποῦ τῶν ἀπορρήτων ἀγαθῶν ἀιδίως ἀπολαύσωσιν, οἱ δὲ ἁμαρτωλοὶ εὑρεθέντες ὡς κακοὶ ἀπορρήτου κολάσεως τεύξονται τὸν αἰῶνα","issue":"Within the clause introduced by ἵνα, the first outcome uses the subjunctive ἀπολαύσωσιν, while the second shifts to the future indicative τεύξονται. The translation treats them as coordinated outcomes without correcting the grammatical shift.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
